findings.what: The curved element at the south-east corner of the Level 2 terrace, with its 0.9 m straight return at x 8.05-8.22, is built as a 3.70 m curved wall (Max object BB_L2_Wall_006). In the default Orbit view it is the object nearest the camera. From the street and from the terrace it towers over the 1.10 m terrace railings on both sides. Every piece of drawing evidence says it is a low parapet. Confirms the builder's open question.
findings.evidence: Drawing: 2 concentric A-WALL ARCs (centre (5.651,-8.274), r 2.425 / 2.575, so 0.15 m thick) plus 4 lines, in the Revit link block. All are colour 8 with no line weight, and there is no fill (poché). The other 199 A-WALL lines in the L2 link block are cut lines (0.25 mm, colour 7), and all other base-building walls have A-WALL-PATT fills. So this is the only wall drawn entirely in projection style, which means it is below the cut plane, i.e. low. The terrace railings (Railing - 100X150, A-FLOR-HRAL) run into both of its ends: the south rail ends at x 5.699, the east rail starts at y -7.338. On L1 there is only the A-FLOR paving outline under it, so nothing could carry a 3.7 m wall. The builder rejected an 'unfilled wall = low wall' rule. That objection is right about fills (the L1 west party wall has unfilled cavity strips), but those strips are drawn with cut lines, so a line-style test separates the two cases. findings.suggestedFix: Add a general builder rule: a wall-layer piece whose faces are all drawn without the layer's cut line weight and that has no fill is below the cut plane. Build it as a parapet at railing height (1.10 m), with follow=false, and list it for the owner. An alternative general rule: an unfilled wall piece whose ends meet railing ends takes the railing height. The owner still confirms the exact height.

findings.what: The Revit 'GLASS WALL 2600H' partitions are built as opaque 3.70 m walls. On Level 1: the manager's room (south and east sides), the meeting room's east side, the BA/BE screen and the lobby screen between the entrance/ATM lobby and the banking hall. On Level 2: the mini bar / wealth room on three sides. Their glass doors (L1-005, L1-007, L1-008, L1-022, L2-010) get opaque lintels from 2.40 to 3.70 m. The 10 mm frameless screen around the double glass door L1-027 (lift hall) is probably glass too. In Max the problem is worse: the L1 glass is fused into BB_L1_Wall_005 (20.24 m2, 87% of all L1 wall area) and the L2 glass into BB_L2_Wall_005 and BB_L2_Wall_010. The 3D team cannot select the glass to change its material or height without splitting splines.
findings.evidence: There are 16 'Basic Wall _ GLASS WALL 2600H 20X100' blocks on A-WALL (11 on L1, 5 on L2), about 8.4 m of glass wall on each level. findings.suggestedFix: Read the Revit wall-type name the same way door heads are read from 'WxH': this is a generic vocabulary rule, so no per-drawing data is needed. A 'Basic Wall' block whose type name contains GLASS is glass, and its height comes from '<n>H' (2600H = 2.60 m). Build it as its own glass part: a 10 mm pane on the hatch inside the block's 100 mm band, with mullion strips at the ends, and nothing above 2.60 m. Lintels over its doors become glass transoms up to 2.60 m. Keep the glass as separate Max objects on BB_<L>_Glass.

findings.what: In the Max script the SE curve (BB_L2_Wall_006) is a 'follow' part. If the 3D team sets its Extrude to a parapet height, pressing 'Update levels and heights' puts it back to the level's wall height.
findings.evidence: Its BB_part call passes follow=true. BB_updateLevels sets ex.amount = newHeights[fi] - base on every part whose BB_follow is true.
findings.suggestedFix: Fixed together with bank-se-parapet-full-height: parapets are built with follow=false. As an extra safeguard, Update could skip objects whose Extrude amount was edited by hand.

findings.what: test_bank.mjs uses fixed port 9377 by default, and the shared cdp.mjs launch() attaches to whatever browser already answers on the debugging port. Two sessions on the same port drive, and finally close, each other's browser, which can give false passes or fails. This happened during this review: a first screenshot run on port 9391 captured the Sukhumvit house page from another session's browser. The run was repeated on a port checked to be free.
findings.evidence: cdp.mjs launch() polls http://127.0.0.1:<port>/json/version, attaches to the first page listed, and close() sends Browser.close to that browser. The builder's runs 4 and 5 took 49 s and 48 s against 23-33 s before, which the builder put down to 'probably the other agent's load'.
findings.suggestedFix: In test_bank.mjs (not shared code), stop with an error if the port already answers before launch, or pick a free port. Changing the shared helper to use --remote-debugging-port=0 with DevToolsActivePort is the owner's decision, since viewer-modes is shared.

RAILINGS: 2 on L1 and 5 on L2, 1.10 m, on the A-FLOR-HRAL lines. The terrace bands are 15 cm wide, not the 5-10 cm the README says.
TERRACE: building it as floor fits the drawing. The L2 louvred doors swing out onto it, the L1 A-FLOR paving outline matches its shape, and its edge is a 100x150 balustrade.
FLOOR PLATES: no floor is missing. The extras are the north-stair floor and the corner bulges; the stair void is not cut.
ROOM NAMES: all 18 are in the correct rooms; only some overlap.

MAX SCRIPT: the 86 BB_part calls match bank_model.json one for one (kind, z0, z1, follow, level). It also builds 4 stair shapes (30/76/87/54 lines) and 18 room texts. Levels are #(0.00,3.70) and heights #(3.70,3.70). The model-data stamp 7bfd8b700cb7 is the same in the JSON, the HTML and the .ms. Layers are named BB_<level>_<kind> as the README says. The script reuses the presidential constructs, adding only per-level arrays, open stair splines and the level update; reading it found no fault. Complexity is close to the presidential script (at most 2 holes per part; 930 vertices against 866). It has not been run in Max, which this review cannot do.

OWNER QUESTIONS: floor-to-floor 3.70 m cannot be checked beyond the 21 risers. 2.40 m for the glass and pivot doors is plausible. The terrace question is answered above; the north stair is a separate finding.
